To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the auxiliary transmembranes domain 1 of YidC is the major contact site for the SecYEG complex, while the globular domain and C1 loop of E. coli and M. tuberculosis YidC are additional contact sites.

the auxiliary transmembrane domain 1 and the globular domain of YidC interact with the SecY and SecE component of the SecYEG complex and that the C1 loop is in contact with both the SecY and the FtsY component of the SRP receptor complex.

the auxiliary transmembranes 1 and 2 of YidC interact with the transmembrane domains 3-6 of the SecYEG complex, while the globular domain and C1 loop of E. coli and T. maritima YidC are involved in contacts with SRP and the FtsY receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that govern membrane protein insertion and targeting.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the insertion of membrane proteins in Escherichia coli and other prokaryotic organisms.
the molecular mechanism of protein targeting and insertion into membranes of eukaryotic cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the auxiliary transmembranes of YidC interact with the lateral gate of the SecY translocon and that the C1 loop interacts with the SRP-target machinery.
the interaction network of the bacterial YidC insertases with the SecY translocon, the SRP and the FtsY is complex and dynamic.
YidC is a highly versatile protein with a large interaction surface that can bind to multiple membrane protein insertion machineries in a highly dynamic manner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
YidC is a multi-tasking membrane protein that interacts with the Sec machinery, the SRP and the ribosome, thereby facilitating the insertion of a wide variety of membrane proteins.
YidC interacts transiently with the SecY translocon and SRP, but more stably with SRP receptor FTSY.
YidC is a highly versatile membrane protein insertase, which can interact with the SecY translocon, the SRP receptor and even with itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
YidC can be in contact with the lateral gate of the SecYEG channel.
YidC interacts simultaneously with the SRP and SecYEG translocases and thus is ideally positioned to coordinate the transfer of nascent membrane proteins from the SecYEG to the SRP receptor.
the auxiliary transmembranes of YidC can be considered as an important contact site for the SecYEG complex and that the YidCs globular domain and C1 loop are involved in the YidC-FesY interaction.
